subject.title: [security] Code portal proxy omits frame-ancestors, allowing same-site clickjacking of isolated Code sessions

question: Should Browser Code proxy responses deny framing by default, or should Crabbox support a narrowly configured ancestor allowlist for operators who intentionally embed Code?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the final policy affects a browser security boundary and could intentionally break unsupported embedding workflows.

options.title: Deny framing by default
options.body: Add `frame-ancestors 'none'` to the Code proxy CSP and treat any embedding support as a separate reviewed feature.

options.title: Add a reviewed allowlist
options.body: Introduce a narrowly documented ancestor policy only if maintainers know of a supported embedding use case and can test the compatibility/security tradeoff.

options.title: Defer pending browser proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a deployed same-site iframe reproduction is supplied before choosing the CSP policy.

recommendation.title: Deny framing by default
recommendation.body: Add `frame-ancestors 'none'` to the Code proxy CSP and treat any embedding support as a separate reviewed feature.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied by git and PR metadata to the current Worker Code portal and adjacent portal security hardening history.
